```{r setup, include=FALSE}

library(tidyverse)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 5,
                      fig.height = 3,
                      out.width = "75%",
                      message = FALSE,
                      fig.align = "center")
options(list(dplyr.summarise.inform = FALSE))

source( here::here( "simulationII/load_master_rerandomization_results.R" ) )

range_dat <- filter( range_dat, Covariates=="best" )
```

We extend our rerandomization simulation analysis to examine how the estimators function for specific scenarios when we operate within estimand.
See the main rerandomizartion report for how the range of estimates across the simulation scenarios changes.

This report shows how the ranges go down when we go from looking at ranges across all estimators to looking at the ranges within the Person or Cluster targeting estimators.



## How do ranges reduce by going within estimand

For each outcome, we can see how the range of the ATE or SE estimates goes down when looking within each estimand (Person or Cluster).
We do this first for the ATE, and then for the SE estimates.

```{r, include=FALSE}
simW <- range_dat %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select( UniqueID, Estimand, runID, ratioSE, rangeATE ) %>%
  pivot_wider( names_from = "Estimand", values_from = c( "rangeATE", "ratioSE" ) ) %>%
  mutate( rat_ATE_C = rangeATE_Cluster / rangeATE_Overall,
          rat_ATE_P = rangeATE_Person / rangeATE_Overall,
          rat_SE_C = ratioSE_Cluster / ratioSE_Overall,
          rat_SE_P = ratioSE_Person / ratioSE_Overall )


ss_W <- filter( simW, runID == "empirical" )
ss_W

simW <- simW %>%
  group_by( UniqueID ) %>%
  summarise( across( c( rat_ATE_C, rat_ATE_P, rat_SE_C, rat_SE_P ), list( mn=mean, sd=sd ) ) )

fin_res <- left_join( ss_W, simW, 
                      by = "UniqueID", suffix = c( "_true", "" ) )

fin_res
names( fin_res ) <- str_replace( names( fin_res ), "Cluster", "C" )
names( fin_res ) <- str_replace( names( fin_res ), "Person", "P" )
names( fin_res ) <- str_replace( names( fin_res ), "Overall", "All" )
```

```{r}
fin_res %>%
  dplyr::select( UniqueID, contains("ATE") ) %>%
  rename_with(~ str_remove(., "ATE_")) %>%
  knitr::kable( digits = 2 )
```

The above table shows, for each dataset, the average fraction of the range of the ATE estimates for the cluster and person estimands relative to the overall range.
The first columns show the reduction in the real empirical results, and the second set of columns show the average reduction in the simulations.
The `sd` columns show how much these numbers vary across the individual simulation runs.


We do the same for the SEs:

```{r}
fin_res %>%
  dplyr::select( UniqueID, contains("SE") ) %>%
  rename_with(~ str_remove(., "SE_")) %>%
  knitr::kable( digits = 2 )
```


And now some viz:

```{r}
names( fin_res )
finW <- fin_res %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c( runID, UniqueID, rangeATE_All, ratioSE_All ),
    names_to="col", values_to="value" ) %>%
  separate_wider_regex( col, 
                        c( measure = ".*", "_", Estimand = "C|P", "_?", sim = ".*" ) ) %>%
  mutate( measure = paste0( measure, sim ) ) %>%
  dplyr::select( -sim ) %>%
  pivot_wider( names_from = measure, values_from = value ) 


ggplot( finW, aes( rat_ATE, rat_ATEmn ) ) +
  facet_wrap( ~ Estimand ) +
  geom_errorbar( aes( ymin=rat_ATEmn-rat_ATEsd, ymax=rat_ATEmn+rat_ATEsd ), width=0, col="grey" ) +
  geom_point() +
  coord_fixed( xlim=c(0,1), ylim=c(0,1) ) +
  geom_abline( slope=1, intercept=0, lty=2 )+
  labs( y = "Simulation",
        x = "Empirical",
        title = "Reduction in ranges across datasets" )

```

We are seeing no strong relationship between how much the range of ATE estimates goes down across the simulations and how much it went down in our empirical data. For the Person estimand, many of the ratios in the simulation tend to be very small, suggesting that the person-weighted estimators are much closer together in the simulation than they are in the actual data.



For the standard errors (note cropping of figure), we are not seeing much reduction in the ratio of largest to smallest standard error when we move to the two estimands.  

```{r}

ggplot( finW, aes( rat_SE, rat_SEmn ) ) +
  facet_wrap( ~ Estimand ) +
    geom_errorbar( aes( ymin=rat_SEmn-rat_SEsd, ymax=rat_SEmn+rat_SEsd ), width=0, col="grey" ) +
  geom_point() +
  #coord_fixed( xlim=c(0.5,1), ylim=c(0.5,1) ) +
  coord_fixed() + 
  geom_abline( slope=1, intercept=0, lty=2 )+
  labs( y = "Simulation (average reduction SE ratio)",
        x = "Empirical (actual reduction SE ratio)",
        title = "Ratio of ratios of SE estimates" )
```
